subject: Summit Analytics - capacity diagnostic & interim hotpatch plan
messages:
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@summit-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity review ahead of renewal

Hi Jordan,

We did a quick internal audit of token usage and KV cache patterns and are seeing sustained GPU utilization in our Dedicated pool above 78% for several weekdays, with brief spikes toward 93% during batch reindex windows. Renewal is up in early October and the product team is nervous about handling Q4 demand.

Can we schedule a short call next week to walk through:
- a quick diagnostic of current GPU utilization by model/route,
- options for short-term burst capacity while we firm up forecast, and
- implications for our upcoming commit (can we add GPUs mid-term?).

I attached a sliced export of their hourly utilization for the last 30 days.

[attachment: usage_report_aug2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

Thanks,
Amelia Ross
Head of Platform Engineering
Summit Analytics
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@summit-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity review ahead of renewal

Amelia —

Thanks for the data dump, this is exactly the kind of signal we want to catch early. Quick notes before a call:

- Initial read: sustained high baseline with short heavy tails suggests prefix/KV cache pressure plus a handful of large-batch jobs during nightly windows.
- Short-term fix: we can provision a 6x burst GPU pool for 90 days (hotpatch) to cover spikes while we do a smoother commit increase. This avoids immediate contract changes but gives headroom.
- Mid-term: recommend a modest commit bump (add 8 A100-equivalent units) with a 60-day phased rollout tied to utilization gates. Commercial options attached.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min diagnostic on Tue 8/24 11:00am PT — we’ll bring ops + runtime SME.
2) If accepted, spin up interim burst within 48–72 hours after call.
3) Follow-up comms with proposal & commercial terms.

I attached a short deck with commit options and preliminary pricing scenarios.

[attachment: proposed_commit_options.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@summit-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity review ahead of renewal — commercial framing

Amelia — Jordan —

Looping in the commercial ask so everyone has visibility. Two practical levers we can offer:

1) 90-day burst (no long-term commit) billed at a slightly elevated rate — quick to activate.
2) Commit addendum: +8 units with a time-limited discount (12% off unit price) if they sign the amendment before 9/15. We can backfill usage credit for any pro-rated days to align billing to activation date if needed.

If Summit is open to a short-term burst + commit amendment, we can draft an addendum and route for signature within 48 hours after acceptance. I attached a working proposal (commercial terms in pages 3–4).

[attachment: MA_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@summit-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity review ahead of renewal — commercial framing

Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks — the plan sounds reasonable. We confirmed with product that the largest spikes are expected around Nov 10–20 for a scheduled reindex plus a marketing-driven Q4 test between Dec 1–7.

We prefer:
- Activate 90-day burst as interim headroom immediately after the diagnostic call,
- Proceed with +8 unit commit amendment (we prefer start date to be the activation date if possible), and
- Can you confirm whether the discount would apply to backdated days if the commit is applied retroactively?

Sharing our internal forecast and the SLO doc here: https://summit-analytics.share.internal/q4-slo (internal link)

[attachment: q4_forecast_2026.xlsx (XLSX, 46KB)]

—Amelia
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@summit-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2026 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity review ahead of renewal — confirmation & next steps

Amelia — thanks for the clarity and the forecast. Confirming next steps and the operational timeline:

1) Diagnostic call scheduled: Tue 2026-08-24 11:00 PT (Jordan, runtime SME, Summit infra).
2) If diagnostic confirms the pattern we saw in the CSV, Redwood will: spin up a 90-day 6x burst pool within 48 hours, and prepare a commit addendum for +8 units.
3) Commercials: Marissa will finalize the amendment with the 12% limited discount (deadline 9/15). We can make the commit start date the activation date; we will request finance to approve pro-rated backfill credits for the days between activation and signature effective date.
4) I created a tracking JIRA for the operational steps and a HubSpot deal link for contract work: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4421 and https://app.hubspot.com/deal/62345/SUM-2026-08-01

Attachments included in thread: usage_report_aug2026.csv, proposed_commit_options.pdf, MA_proposal_v2.pdf, q4_forecast_2026.xlsx

If that aligns, Marissa — please route the amendment and Karthik — can you flag any SRE constraints for the burst activation window?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
